note: What the pages publish, and the sentence in this repository that backs each one. Read by decision_evals.claims (which refuses a page whose figure no longer resolves to its source) and by the pages themselves (which render `value`). One file, two readers, so the page and the check cannot drift apart. It is not in pyproject.toml because TypeScript cannot read TOML without another dependency, and a generated second copy would recreate the disagreement this design exists to prevent. `source` paths are repository-relative; `quote` is compared after markdown emphasis is stripped and whitespace collapsed, so a hard-wrapped sentence still matches.

claims.why: The ledger's own running total. It is quoted rather than derived because results/triggers/ holds rescored rows that say no call was made, because 6,825 line-counted rows and this figure count different sets, and because STATUS.md corrects by appending -- deriving an integer would force those appended corrections rewritten in place, and they are the evidence itself. This was ~[0-9],[0-9]{3} until 2026-08-19, when an adversarial review appended ~10,062 in the file's own correction format and the gate went green: four digits cannot match five, so the last match stayed ~8,514 and the page would have gone on publishing a superseded total. The same pattern was also blind to a correction written without the tilde, which is how STATUS.md:97 already writes one. Widening it to any thousands-separated number then landed on a per-run 1,548 and refused with the wrong figure named. So it is anchored instead: STATUS.md states a running total in exactly two forms, a 'new total' table row and the prose 'the total is', and group 1 captures the figure so the anchor does not become part of what is compared. Verified against the live file -- it finds ~4,816 then ~8,514, and catches both appended corrections above.

claims.quote: eleven measurements were caught being broken
claims.why: The count of our own instruments caught reading something that was not there. It grows whenever one is found, and three living documents already disagree about it — RESEARCH_PROGRAMME.md says ten, METHODS.md says around eleven, the issue template says eight. STATUS.md is the ledger, so it is the one anchor, and the page must not become a fourth answer.

claims.quote: ran on a corpus that is 89% solvable by counting words
claims.why: The caveat that qualifies every trigger number published before 2026-08-18, and the least flattering figure on the site. A page that quietly softened it would be the one drift nobody reports, so it is anchored to the sentence in SCORECARD.md that states it in full.

claims.quote: So every result above was competing for about **nine points over a ruler**.
claims.why: How much room the arms were ever fighting over. It read `about six points` until 2026-08-13, when the checkpoints were reconciled and the six-point figure turned out to be arithmetic across two answer keys. The superseded phrase is in the retractions below; this is the live one, and pinning it is what stops the page drifting back.

claims.quote: eight trivial features reads 0.7054 against a majority baseline of 0.6667
claims.why: The best a model-free shortcut does on the rebuilt corpus, and the number that says the rebuild worked. The page prints it rounded, so the rounding is declared rather than done by hand: `0.71` has to be what `0.7054` rounds to, and a corpus revision that moved the stump would refuse here instead of leaving a stale two-digit figure that still looks right.

retractions.quote: This read "0.956 … about six points" until the checkpoints were reconciled.
retractions.why: The figure compared a version 2 ruler with a version 1 arm, and 0.956 was not the best arm at either version. The live figure is nine points; see the `headroom-points` claim.

retractions.quote: Routes to one of six procedures depending on what is actually hard about the decision
retractions.why: The skill routes to six procedures, not four. `council.md` and `hinge.md` shipped on 2026-08-19 and the landing page went on offering four, which is the drift this whole register was written for.
